clue.text: Drawing room goddess left — that is right

blocks.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin
L is the standard abbreviation for left
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone describes a drawing room's decor: a statue of a goddess on the left, and that is exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing room' reads as a parlour, but here it is literally a room for drawing in. 'that is' and 'right' are both wordplay, so there are no link words at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's studio is a workroom where drawing and painting are done, hence a room for drawing.

clue.text: Non-U man, old school worker for instance?

definitions.note: a worker ant is one example

indicators.note: non- before a letter means without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a man's name containing the letter U to lose
O is the abbreviation for old
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A man who is not upper class, from an old school, does the work, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is a British term for not upper class, but here it means remove U. A worker is an ant, which is an insect and so an arthropod.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthropods are invertebrates with jointed legs, including insects such as the worker ant.

clue.text: Running water locally, woman endlessly causes pain

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the woman's name is dropped

blocks.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or stream
a woman's name

explanation.surface: Running water near a woman's home, which never stops, is giving her pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a regional word: ea is northern English dialect for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear, a specific kind of ache.

clue.text: Eating this up vegan makes vegetarian furious

indicators.note: the vegan word is eating, that is surrounding, something; take it away and only the eaten part is left
up in a down light means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: the word whose middle is wanted
its letters wrap the middle of vegetarian
this stands for the answer itself

explanation.surface: A vegan eating this turns vegetarian, which makes someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as a sum: VEG + this upside down + AN = VEGETARIAN. So take VEGAN out of VEGETARIAN, leaving ETARI, and turn it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a synonym for angry, very cross.

clue.text: Socialist penning article on yen to hand

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, so the socialist word holds the article

blocks.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a is the indefinite article
Y is the symbol for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A socialist writing an article on the yen keeps it to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'on' means placed after, so Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready, as in ready cash, means available and to hand for immediate use.

clue.text: Doctor says our bones are here

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the following letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A doctor points to an X-ray and tells us where our bones are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the speaker, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossuary is a container or chamber where the skeletal remains of the dead are stored.

clue.text: Worn by tense, macho types, uniform available

blocks.note: clothes worn by someone are on them
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
he-men are muscular, macho men
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A uniform is being worn by tense, macho men who are available.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the menu is offered and so available, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Sailor binding leg — old man up for procedure across the Atlantic?

definitions.note: the American name for the procedure

indicators.note: binding means tying round, so the sailor word encloses the leg word
up in a down light means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor
pins is slang for legs
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A sailor's leg is bound up, and his old father goes into surgery in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Procedure across the Atlantic' is a lumbar puncture, called a spinal tap in the US; the question mark nods to the comedy film too.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal tap is the American term for a lumbar puncture, drawing fluid from the spine.

clue.text: Belly when wobbling bad sign

indicators.note: something wobbling is unsteady and shifting, so its letters move about

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A wobbling belly is a bad sign for one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the everyday word for the abdomen, the part of the body holding the stomach.

clue.text: Support given about engaging eastern poet

indicators.note: turned about means facing the opposite way, so the support word is written backwards
engaging means taking in or holding, so the reversed word encloses the next letter

blocks.note: a stay is a prop or support, as in a ship's rigging
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Support is given to an eastern poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.

clue.text: Designate range and theatre for Spitfire

blocks.note: to term something is to name or designate it
an Aga is a make of kitchen range, a large cast-iron cooker
NT is the National Theatre in London; 'and' simply joins

explanation.surface: Someone is choosing a firing range and a theatre of war for a Spitfire fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second World War plane is a decoy: a spitfire is also a fiery-tempered person. An Aga is the classic British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing, quarrelsome woman, which is what a spitfire describes.

clue.text: Home help in retreat in country I may represent

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word for help is read from its end

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper retreats to a country where they may represent themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition has a second layer: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter I is represented by the word India.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country, and its name is the radio code word that stands for the letter I.

clue.text: Keith Richards for one back in untidy heap in garden

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: Keith Richards, guitarist of the Rolling Stones, is a rock musician
the final letter of untidy

explanation.surface: Keith Richards is found lying back in an untidy heap in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy heap' tempts you to rearrange HEAP, but untidy only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is an ornamental mound of stones in a garden, planted with alpines, so a heap in a garden.

clue.text: Times letters from Greek theologian

blocks.note: eras are times or periods
mu is a Greek letter; two of them are mus

explanation.surface: A newspaper, The Times, prints letters from a Greek theologian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is just the plural of a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Dutch Renaissance humanist and Catholic theologian.

clue.text: Divine environment for ace crew testing position?

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever lives in it, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: to divine is to foresee or predict
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a crew is a body of men

explanation.surface: A heavenly setting for an ace aircrew undergoing tests at their station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as an adjective, heavenly, but it is the verb meaning to foretell. A and MEN go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A predicament is a difficult or trying situation, so a testing position to be in.

clue.text: Header missed by Midlands team kid, embarrassed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and missing it means it is left off

blocks.note: Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club, known as Villa
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A youngster in a Midlands football team misses a header and is embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header' sounds like football, fitting the team, but it means the first letter. The Midlands is a region of central England around Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ill at ease is to feel awkward or uncomfortable, as an embarrassed person does.

clue.text: Sudden attack advanced: bishop into wine endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, the wine's name loses its final letter
into means going inside, so the bishop goes inside the wine

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire
B is bishop in chess notation

explanation.surface: A sudden attack advanced as a bishop got endlessly into the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an old word for an ambush, a surprise attack from hiding.

clue.text: Brandy measure bargain, reduced by shilling

indicators.note: reduced by means made smaller by taking away the thing named next

blocks.note: a snip is a bargain, something cheap
S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A measure of brandy is a bargain, reduced in price by a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth a twentieth of a pound; it was abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small drink of spirits, the sort of measure poured of brandy.

clue.text: Pence rates may vary in cash dispenser?

definitions.note: a person rather than a machine, hence the question mark

indicators.note: to vary is to change, so these letters change their order

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for pence
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Exchange rates for pence may vary in a cash machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash dispenser' suggests an ATM, but it is the official who hands out wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A paymaster is the person responsible for paying out money, such as wages, so literally dispenses cash.

clue.text: Vicious, perhaps making comeback, underworld figure

indicators.note: to make a comeback is to come back, so the name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Sid Vicious was the bass player of the Sex Pistols

explanation.surface: A vicious villain, possibly a gangster, makes a comeback in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' looks like an adjective and 'underworld figure' like a gangster; the first is the punk rocker's surname, the second a Roman god.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman god of the dead and ruler of the underworld, equivalent to Pluto.

clue.text: Southern Irish king — alpha male in Ireland — runs as leader

indicators.note: in places the preceding phrase inside the name of the country that follows

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
Ir is the abbreviation for Irish
K is king in chess notation
Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an alpha is the brightest star in a constellation
M is the abbreviation for male
R is runs in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A southern Irish king, top dog in Ireland, stands as the leader of his people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs as leader' sounds like standing for office, but runs is cricket's R and only 'leader' is the definition. An alpha is a constellation's brightest star.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Keir Starmer has led the British Labour Party since 2020 and became Prime Minister in 2024.

clue.text: Work hard, play hard for 19 28's organisation

blocks.note: to labour is to work hard
to party is to celebrate and play hard

explanation.surface: Work hard, play hard: a motto handed down for a leader's organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Starmer, the answer to 19 and 28, leads the Labour Party, the British political organisation.

clue.text: Iceland's outlying territory taking a practical view

indicators.note: outlying means on the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
taking in means holding inside, so the territory wraps around the letters

blocks.note: a realm is a kingdom or territory
the first and last letters of Iceland's

explanation.surface: Iceland's outlying territory is managed in a practical way.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the attitude of accepting things as they are and dealing with them practically.

clue.text: Jumps over fences initially under cloud

indicators.note: over in a down light or turned over means read backwards, here the word for jumps
initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it
a fence encloses ground, so the first part surrounds the next letter

blocks.note: starts are sudden jumps, as when startled
the first letter of under

explanation.surface: A horse jumps over the fences in a race run under low cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumps over fences' reads as a steeplechase, but jumps is a noun (starts) read backwards, and fences means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat, grey layer of cloud covering the sky.

clue.text: Violent disturbance to one side in sadomasochism

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: S and M, or S&M, is the abbreviation for sadomasochism
taken as written
right is one side, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A violent outburst takes place on one side in a sadomasochistic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a violent outburst, of weather or of emotion, a turbulent upheaval.

clue.text: Exceptional bat must carry John around Cypriot city

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word for John is read backwards
to carry something is to hold it inside, so the batsman's name wraps the next part

blocks.note: Brian Lara, the West Indian batsman, holds Test and first-class scoring records
john and can are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A star batsman has to take someone called John on a tour round a city in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name, but it is slang for a lavatory, as is can.
explanation.definitionFit: Larnaca is a port city on the south coast of Cyprus, home to the island's main airport.

clue.text: Somewhat leggy stripper almost in place?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an insect with long hind legs that strips crops bare

explanation.surface: A rather leggy stripper is nearly in position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' suggests a dancer; it is the insect whose swarms strip fields of vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place and is used in English for a particular position or site.

clue.text: Dish from 10 8 for example read out?

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so the word is taken by how it is said

blocks.note: the poet at 8 is an example of a writer

explanation.surface: A dish from somewhere, mentioned as an example, is read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is INDIA and 8 is YEATS; a non-rhotic speaker says 'writer' much like the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or other vegetables and spices.

clue.text: Round piano with English artist for Fidelio?

definitions.note: the question mark marks Fidelio as one example

blocks.note: O is round in shape
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
E is the abbreviation for English; 'with' joins
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A round of piano music played with an English artist for a performance of Fidelio.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera, so it is an example of the musical-dramatic form.

clue.text: This vicar turns out to be the record-holder?

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned about and come out in a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply all nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: This vicar turns out to have set some sort of record.
explanation.walkthrough: Record-holder suggests a champion, but it is someone who literally holds records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archivist is the person who keeps and looks after historical documents and records.

clue.text: Woman the French name in calamitous experience

indicators.note: in puts the preceding letters inside the word for a disaster

blocks.note: a mare, short for nightmare, is British slang for a disastrous time
le is French for 'the'
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A woman finds her French name in the middle of a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'have a mare' is British slang for having a nightmare of a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene is a female given name, as in the actress Marlene Dietrich.
